page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply and divide by 7
steps.margin_note: First mark. The power is 7x, so the denominator must be 7x as well. Multiplying and dividing by 7 supplies it without changing the value.
steps.memory_tip: The number in the power comes out in front. Put 7x below, take 7 outside.
lines: Putting x = 0 gives 0/0, so the expression is rewritten first.
The power is 7x, so the denominator is made 7x:

steps.why: The standard limit is (eᵗ − 1)/t → 1, and it only applies when the denominator is exactly the power. Multiplying and dividing by 7 changes nothing in value but puts the expression in that shape.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer as 1 by treating (e⁷ˣ − 1)/x as already standard.
Dividing by 7 outside as well, which cancels the factor that should be kept.

steps.label: Apply (eᵗ − 1)/t → 1
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put t = 7x and say that t → 0 as x → 0. The limit is then 1, and the 7 outside is the answer.
steps.memory_tip: For (e^(kx) − 1)/x the answer is just k. Here k is 7.

recall.must_convey: That with t = 7x the standard limit gives 1, so the value is 7.

steps.why: Naming the substitution and saying t → 0 is what makes the standard limit apply. The 7 was taken outside at the previous step, so it is untouched by the limit and stands as the answer.
common_mistakes: Giving 1 as the answer by forgetting the 7 taken outside.
Writing e⁷ as the answer by substituting x = 1 instead of taking a limit.

insider_note: Make the denominator match the power: write it as 7 · (e⁷ˣ − 1)/(7x). The 7 pulled out front IS the answer, since the bracket goes to 1.
